clue.text: Piece I have taken with pawn in retaliation

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective: a punitive strike is one made in retaliation

blocks.note: P is the chess abbreviation for a pawn
a unit is a single piece of a set
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A chess player captures a piece with a pawn as revenge for an earlier loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'Piece' look like a chessman, but it is just a unit, and the pawn goes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Punitive means inflicting punishment, which is what is dealt out by way of retaliation.

clue.text: Help actor in play, in small part

indicators.note: one word sits in the other, placed inside it

blocks.note: pt is the short form of part
to romp is to play boisterously

explanation.surface: A minor performer helps out a fellow actor who has forgotten lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'part' both look theatrical, but play is a verb for frolicking and the small part is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt is to feed a forgotten line to an actor on stage.

clue.text: Servant whose charges are small but growing

definitions.text: Servant whose charges are small but growing

blocks.note: surface reading: fees that are modest but rising
setter's reading: the young children in a servant's care

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests fees going up; they are children, who are small and still growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a domestic employed to look after young children.

clue.text: Loyal kid, finding bone to pick?

blocks.note: true means faithful
to kid and to rib both mean to tease

explanation.surface: A faithful child finds a bone to gnaw at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease; 'bone to pick' adds a playful picture of picking a rib clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A true rib is one of the upper seven ribs joined directly to the breastbone, a bone one might pick at.

clue.text: Spring over, store things here

blocks.note: first meaning: to leap over something using the hands
second meaning: a secure strongroom or cellar

explanation.surface: Advice to jump across and keep your belongings in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Vault is both a verb for leaping with support and a noun for a secure storage room.

clue.text: Parking in Asian city where one used to go for cryptic advice

definitions.text: where one used to go for cryptic advice

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

blocks.note: the capital region of India
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A traveller looks for a parking spot in a crowded Asian city famed for an oracle.
explanation.walkthrough: The oracle at Delphi in ancient Greece gave famously ambiguous answers, hence 'cryptic advice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the site of the ancient Greek oracle, whose pronouncements were notoriously riddling.

clue.text: Large amount of earth is turned over in area contaminated with uranium

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the short word is read backwards
contaminated means corrupted, so these letters are spoiled into a new order
one part sits in the other, placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Soil is dug over in an area polluted by radioactive waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' reads as soil, but it is the planet: the definition is a huge land mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia, Europe and Asia combined, is the largest continuous land mass on the planet.

clue.text: Bishop, for instance, making ceasefire announcement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a ceasefire brings peace

explanation.surface: A churchman declares a truce.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is a chessman, not a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the pieces on a chessboard, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Hard work at home needing clean after river comes in

indicators.note: a word that comes in enters another and sits inside it

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
something dusty needs cleaning
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Housework at home after a river floods in and leaves a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing' looks like a link but is part of the description of the dusty state.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means diligence, steady hard work, as in a person's industry.

clue.text: Error not pronounced — it's easily undone

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a slip is a small mistake
the word is said, giving a same-sounding tie

explanation.surface: A mistake that is not obvious is easy to correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not pronounced' looks like 'not noticeable'; it means say the word not.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip knot is designed to come apart with a single pull.

clue.text: Work by Dickens, whom we both like

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of Charles Dickens's last completed novel
second meaning: a person known and liked by two of us

explanation.surface: Two people discover they share a favourite Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title is also the everyday phrase for a friend that two people have in common.

clue.text: French clown and I go off course in vessel

indicators.note: the letters are put in the vessel, so they sit inside its word

blocks.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking
taken as written
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A clown and a companion drift off course in a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat in the surface, but it is a pot holding the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the stock sad clown of French pantomime, in loose white costume.

clue.text: Have legal support groups succeeded?

blocks.note: posses are bands summoned to help a sheriff enforce the law
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A question about whether groups backing a court case have won.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have or own it; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pub and its front I preserve in centre of London

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
the first letter of the pub word just found
taken as written
to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A publican sets about preserving a pub's frontage in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' is literal: the Barbican Centre is a large arts complex in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbican is an arts centre and housing estate in the City, so it is a London centre.

clue.text: Conservative leading committee is part of the furniture

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a team that is up is ahead
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A Tory chairing a committee is a fixture there, always present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of the furniture' is the idiom for someone always around; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is literally an item of furniture, rather than a long-serving person.

clue.text: Tree in shot taken from garrison town

indicators.note: something taken from a word is removed, leaving the rest

blocks.note: Aldershot in Hampshire is the traditional home of the British Army
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree appears in a photograph taken from a military town.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is an English town long known as the home of the British Army; drop its shot and a tree is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Was pleasantly distracted by natural light

definitions.text: Was pleasantly distracted by natural light

blocks.note: surface reading: someone's attention wandered agreeably
setter's reading: daylight, so the musing happened in the daytime

explanation.walkthrough: Natural light suggests a sunbeam catching the eye; read it as the time of day when the reverie happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to drift into pleasant reverie while awake, as in the day.

clue.text: Having a consecrated property husband let

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A husband lets out a church building he owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' and 'let' suggest renting; property means a quality and let means permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy, so it describes something with a sacred quality.

clue.text: Range in Patagonian Desert, which it bounds

indicators.note: the answer is found lying in the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second
surface padding: a true geographical aside about the mountains edging the desert

explanation.surface: A geography note: a mountain range forms the edge of the Patagonian Desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'which it bounds' is true to life: the mountains form the desert's western edge, making the clue nearly self-describing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the great mountain range running down the west of South America.

clue.text: Container of schoolbooks the class endlessly rearranged

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is cut
rearranged means put in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher reshuffles the class's schoolbag arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag of the kind traditionally used to carry school books.

clue.text: Nominal inheritance, misguided on my part

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so these letters go the wrong way into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits a mistaken bequest was their own error.
explanation.definitionFit: A patronym is a name derived from one's father, so it is a name inherited.

clue.text: Strange condition — one remains if twin daughters and sons leave

indicators.note: the letters leave the answer, so working backwards they were sitting inside the remainder

blocks.note: taken as written: what is left at the end
D is the abbreviation for daughter, and twins make two of them
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural
surface wording: names the word left over once the others go

explanation.surface: A family puzzle: when the twins and the boys move out, one child is left at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take two Ds and two Ss out of the answer and ONE is what remains, so the answer is ONE with them put back.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddness is the state or quality of being strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Event in Edinburgh that's superficially artistic?

blocks.note: first meaning: the military music display held each summer at Edinburgh Castle
second meaning: a design inked into the skin, art on the surface

explanation.surface: A sceptic suggests the Edinburgh show is only skin-deep culture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous yearly show of bands and drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattoo names both a military evening display and a picture inked into the skin, art on the body's surface.

clue.text: Lion pierced by wayward shot in part of Africa

indicators.note: something pierced has another thing driven into its middle
wayward means unruly and straying, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter's stray bullet wounds a lion somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Mess initially put together by soldiers

blocks.clueFragment: Mess initially put together by soldiers
blocks.note: surface reading: an army mess hall first assembled by troops
setter's reading: a word built from first letters, an acronym coined by soldiers for chaos

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' suggests a soldiers' dining hall; it means a muddle. The answer is a Second World War army acronym, 'Situation Normal: All Fouled Up' in polite form.
explanation.definitionFit: The army slang term for a chaotic, botched situation is a synonym for a mess.

clue.text: At least one of two leaders in really autonomous principality

indicators.note: the leaders are the words' front-runners, so only their opening letters are kept

blocks.note: and/or means either or both of two options
the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A political remark about a principality ruled by two co-princes.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Andorra really does have two heads of state, the French president and the Bishop of Urgell.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: City of famous mausoleum containing old Greek meeting-place

indicators.note: the city's word holds the next item inside it

blocks.note: Agra in India is home to the Taj Mahal
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old Greek forum sits within the city of a famous tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open public square of an ancient Greek city, used for assemblies.

clue.text: Met expectations?

blocks.note: surface reading: lived up to what was hoped for
setter's reading: the Met Office, Britain's national weather service, and what it expects to happen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like the past of meet; it is the Met Office, the UK weather service, whose expectations are its predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast is precisely what the Met Office expects the weather to do.

clue.text: Like a score of ten from perfect substitute

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: twenty is twice ten

blocks.note: first meaning: a score is twenty, twice the size of ten
second meaning: a lookalike who stands in for someone

explanation.surface: A judge's mark of ten falling short of a perfect score.
explanation.walkthrough: A score here is the number twenty, not a mark out of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is twice ten, and a stand-in who exactly resembles someone is called their double.

clue.text: Shrill voice of loud singer introducing song sequence

indicators.note: the singer is introducing, that is bringing in, the next item inside itself

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an alto is a singer of the low female or high male range
a set is a run of songs played in one go

explanation.surface: A loud singer opens a run of songs in a piercing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register of a male voice, thin and shrill.
